components.css: .ds-pen{display:grid;grid-template-columns:auto 1fr auto;gap:.75rem;align-items:center;font-family:var(--label);font-size:.95rem;color:var(--ink-2)}.ds-pen input{width:100%;margin:0;height:2.25rem;background:transparent;appearance:none;-webkit-appearance:none;cursor:ew-resize}.ds-pen input::-webkit-slider-runnable-track{height:2px;background:var(--ink)}.ds-pen input::-moz-range-track{height:2px;background:var(--ink)}.ds-pen input::-webkit-slider-thumb{-webkit-appearance:none;width:14px;height:30px;margin-top:-14px;border-radius:7px 7px 2px 2px;background:var(--pen);border:2px solid var(--paper);box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgb(23 33 28 / .35)}.ds-pen input::-moz-range-thumb{width:12px;height:28px;border-radius:7px 7px 2px 2px;background:var(--pen);border:2px solid var(--paper);box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgb(23 33 28 / .35)}.ds-pen input:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--pen);outline-offset:3px}.ds-pen button{font:inherit;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;border:1px solid var(--ink);background:var(--paper);color:var(--ink);padding:.35rem .6rem;cursor:pointer}.ds-pen button:hover{background:var(--ink);color:var(--paper)}

components.css: .ds-rail ol{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;border-left:1px solid var(--ink);background:var(--paper)}.ds-rail a{display:block;position:relative;padding:.4rem 0 .4rem .9rem;font-family:var(--label);font-weight:600;font-size:.95rem;letter-spacing:.07em;text-transform:uppercase;text-decoration:none;color:var(--ink-2)}.ds-rail a span{display:inline-block;width:1.1rem;color:var(--ink)}.ds-rail a::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:-1px;top:50%;width:.6rem;height:2px;background:var(--pen);transform:scaleX(0);transform-origin:left;transition:transform .4s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)}.ds-rail a:hover{color:var(--ink)}.ds-rail a[aria-current="true"]{color:var(--pen)}.ds-rail a[aria-current="true"]::before{transform:scaleX(1)}.ds-rail a:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--pen);outline-offset:3px}

narrative.overview:
The site is a river-stage recorder sheet: pale green ruled chart paper, graphite ink, and two recorder pens. Pen 1 (carmine) draws the flood front against the clock; pen 2 (recorder blue) marks what was actually observed. Everything else is graphite on paper. The reading is that of an instrument record, not a story map: hairline frames, boxed caps name plates bolted onto the thing they name, tabular figures for every reading, and a serif column for the argument.

Density is that of a well-set scientific report: generous reading measure, figures that sit as framed plates in the column, a sticky contents rail down the ruled left margin. Ground is always light (read at desks and on phones in daylight). Depth comes from rules and frames, not from shadow or tone; the only colour that shouts is the carmine pen, and it shouts about one thing.

The world rejects the dark satellite story map with stat cards. The map itself is a hillshade inked in the paper's own greens; satellite imagery is an opt-in layer, not the ground.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled chart paper (8px minor, 40px major) in the frame and on chart plates, never behind running text.
One committed spot colour (carmine pen) for the front, our footprint and the cursor; recorder blue only for observations and Copernicus.
Optical, radar and both as 45°, −45° and crossed hatches.
Condensed grotesk caps for plates, station heads and readings; a serif reading face for prose.
Square corners and 1px graphite frames throughout; 3px graphite top rules open every major band.

rules.name: The Two Pens Rule
rules.body: Carmine means the front, our footprint, or the cursor. Blue means observed, or Copernicus. Nothing else gets a pen: alerts, warning minutes, open-data counts and every structural mark are graphite.

rules.name: The Exposure Hatch Rule
rules.body: Optical change is a carmine 45° hatch on carmine wash; radar change is a blue −45° hatch on blue wash; "both" is the two hatches crossed. A legend swatch carries the same hatch as the mark it explains.

rules.name: The Tabular Reading Rule
rules.body: Every number a reader might compare (tables, readouts, axis values, bar ends) is set with tabular lining figures.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: The serif never sets a label, and the condensed grotesk never sets a paragraph.

rules.name: The Ruled Frame Rule
rules.body: The chart-paper ruling belongs to the frame (the rail column) and to chart plates without a numeric axis. A chart with a numeric axis (the trace, flat charts, the warning-minute bars) turns the CSS ruling off and draws its own ruling on its data scale inside the SVG, so every line means a unit. Running text never sits on ruling.

rules.name: The Frame, Not Float Rule
rules.body: Plates, charts, maps, tables and controls never lift. If it is part of the record it is framed, not shadowed.

dos: Do keep carmine for the front, our footprint and the cursor, and blue for observations and Copernicus; set everything else in graphite.
Do draw ruling on the data scale inside any chart with a numeric axis, and switch the CSS ruling off for it.
Do encode optical, radar and both as 45°, −45° and crossed hatches, with matching legend swatches.
Do frame plates, charts, maps and tables with 1px graphite and open bands with a 2–3px graphite rule.
Do set every compared number in tabular lining figures.
Do keep ink-3 to strokes and large text.
donts: Don't put chart-paper ruling behind running text.
Don't use a pen colour for alerts, warning minutes or any structural mark.
Don't introduce a dark ground or a satellite basemap as the default map ground.
Don't round corners on plates, controls, charts, maps or tooltips.
Don't lift record surfaces with shadows; shadows are for floating tips and held controls only.
Don't set paragraphs in the condensed face or labels in the serif.
